title: Type 2 diabetes: outpatient management
subject: endocrinology
summary: Aim for HbA1c below 7% in most adults, start metformin with lifestyle change, add SGLT2 inhibitors or GLP-1 RAs for ASCVD, heart failure, CKD or obesity irrespective of HbA1c, start basal insulin at 10 units or 0.1 to 0.2 units/kg when needed, and screen yearly for complications.

sections.title: Diagnose and assess
items: Diagnosis: HbA1c 6.5% or more, fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or more, 2-hour OGTT glucose 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or more, or random glucose 200 mg/dL or more with classic symptoms. Without unequivocal hyperglycaemia, confirm with a second abnormal test.
Consider type 1 diabetes or LADA if lean, rapid weight loss, ketosis or young onset; consider pancreatic diabetes (fibrocalculous pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis) in India.

At baseline record: weight and BMI, BP, HbA1c, lipids, eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), liver enzymes, ECG, eye and foot examination, ASCVD and heart failure history, hypoglycaemia risk, cost and access.
Check HbA1c at least twice a year when at goal, and every 3 months when not at goal or after treatment changes.

sections.title: Targets
items: HbA1c below 7% (53 mmol/mol) for many non-pregnant adults; below 6.5% if achievable safely (short duration, low hypoglycaemia risk); less stringent goals for frailty, cognitive impairment, limited life expectancy or high hypoglycaemia risk.
CGM users: time in range 70 to 180 mg/dL above 70%; time below 70 mg/dL under 4% (under 1% in older adults) and below 54 mg/dL under 1%.
BP below 130/80 mmHg if safely attainable (systolic below 120 encouraged in high cardiovascular or kidney risk).
LDL cholesterol below 70 mg/dL (1.8 mmol/L) at higher cardiovascular risk aged 40 to 75; below 55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L) with established ASCVD.

sections.title: First-line and organ-protective drugs
items: Lifestyle, weight management and structured diabetes education for all. Start metformin with lifestyle measures at diagnosis unless contraindicated or not tolerated (RSSDI).
Consider initial combination therapy to reach goals faster, especially if HbA1c is more than 1.5% above target.
Established or high risk of ASCVD: add a GLP-1 RA and/or SGLT2 inhibitor with proven cardiovascular benefit, irrespective of HbA1c.
Heart failure (reduced or preserved EF): SGLT2 inhibitor irrespective of HbA1c. Obesity with symptomatic HFpEF: tirzepatide or semaglutide.

CKD (eGFR 20 to 60 and/or albuminuria): SGLT2 inhibitor (start if eGFR 20 or more, continue until kidney failure) and/or a GLP-1 RA with proven kidney benefit. eGFR below 30: GLP-1 RA is preferred for glucose lowering.
Obesity: prioritise agents with high weight efficacy (tirzepatide, semaglutide). MASLD or MASH: GLP-1 RA preferred; pioglitazone or tirzepatide are alternatives.

sections.title: Intensification and insulin
items: Review every 3 to 6 months and intensify without delay. Each added oral class lowers HbA1c about 0.7 to 1.0%; GLP-1 RA or tirzepatide about 1 to 2% or more.

Where cost is a barrier, metformin, sulfonylureas (gliclazide, glimepiride), pioglitazone and human insulin are lower-cost options; DPP-4 inhibitors suit older adults at hypoglycaemia risk. Do not combine a DPP-4 inhibitor with a GLP-1 RA.
Start insulin if there are symptoms of hyperglycaemia or catabolism, HbA1c above 10% or glucose 300 mg/dL (16.7 mmol/L) or more, or ketosis. Otherwise GLP-1 based therapy is preferred before insulin.

Basal insulin: 10 units or 0.1 to 0.2 units/kg/day at bedtime (RSSDI: 0.2 to 0.3 units/kg if HbA1c above 8%); titrate by 2 units every 3 days to the fasting goal (RSSDI: below 115 mg/dL); reduce 10 to 20% after any glucose below 70 mg/dL.
Continue metformin, SGLT2 inhibitor and GLP-1 RA when insulin starts; reduce or stop sulfonylureas when prandial insulin is added.

If HbA1c stays high despite a titrated fasting glucose, or basal exceeds about 0.5 units/kg/day with a bedtime-to-morning drop of 50 mg/dL or more (overbasalisation): add a GLP-1 RA, or prandial insulin 4 units or 10% of the basal dose at the largest meal, or switch to twice-daily premixed insulin.

sections.title: Cardiovascular and kidney protection
items: Statin for all aged 40 to 75: moderate intensity if no ASCVD; high intensity if additional risk factors or ASCVD. Add ezetimibe if LDL goal is not met on the maximum tolerated statin.

BP 130/80 mmHg or more: start treatment. ACE inhibitor or ARB first-line with albuminuria or coronary disease, titrated to the maximum tolerated dose if UACR is 300 mg/g or more or eGFR below 60. Never combine ACE inhibitor with ARB.
Aspirin 75 to 162 mg/day for secondary prevention (clopidogrel 75 mg/day if allergic); for primary prevention only after discussing bleeding risk.
Stop smoking; check potassium and creatinine after starting ACE inhibitors, ARBs or MRAs.

sections.title: Complication screening
items: Kidney: UACR and eGFR at least yearly from diagnosis; 1 to 4 times a year once CKD is present.

Eyes: dilated retinal examination at diagnosis; then every 1 to 2 years if no retinopathy and good control, at least yearly if any retinopathy. Retinal photography or approved AI screening programmes are acceptable. Refer promptly for macular oedema, moderate or worse NPDR, or PDR.

Feet: comprehensive foot examination at least yearly with 10-g monofilament plus one of pinprick, temperature or 128-Hz vibration, and pedal pulses; inspect feet at every visit if sensation is lost or there was a prior ulcer or amputation.
Neuropathy (including autonomic) from diagnosis and yearly. Lipid profile at diagnosis and yearly; BP at every visit; periodic vitamin B12 on long-term metformin.

sections.title: Drug safety
items: Metformin: do not start if eGFR below 45; halve the dose at eGFR 30 to 45 (RSSDI); stop below 30. Hold during dehydrating illness or AKI.

SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycotic infections, volume depletion and euglycaemic DKA. Teach sick-day rules: pause during vomiting, poor intake or acute illness, avoid ketogenic diets, and stop 3 days before surgery.
GLP-1 RA and tirzepatide: nausea, vomiting; titrate slowly; avoid with personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN2; reassess insulin and sulfonylurea doses when starting.
Sulfonylureas: hypoglycaemia risk highest in older adults and CKD; prefer gliclazide or glimepiride over glibenclamide. Pioglitazone: avoid in heart failure (fluid retention).
Women of childbearing potential: counsel on contraception and plan pregnancy; most non-insulin agents are stopped before conception.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Therapeutic inertia: leaving HbA1c above goal for months without intensifying.
Withholding SGLT2 inhibitors or GLP-1 RAs in ASCVD, heart failure or CKD because HbA1c is already at goal.
Adding drugs without reducing sulfonylurea or insulin, causing hypoglycaemia.
Missing albuminuria by checking only serum creatinine.

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally once or twice daily with meals, titrated every 1 to 2 weeks to 1000 mg twice daily (usual maximum 2000 mg/day); extended-release once daily
drugs.notes: Do not start if eGFR below 45; halve at eGFR 30 to 45; stop below 30. Check vitamin B12 periodically.

drugs.name: Empagliflozin
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally once daily (25 mg for extra glucose lowering if eGFR allows)
drugs.notes: HF, CKD and ASCVD benefit; start if eGFR 20 or more. Glucose effect falls below eGFR 45.

drugs.name: Dapagliflozin
drugs.notes: HF and CKD benefit; start if eGFR 20 or more.

drugs.name: Semaglutide (SC)
drugs.dose: 0.25 mg SC once weekly for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly; increase to 1 mg and then 2 mg weekly after at least 4 weeks each if needed
drugs.notes: Oral semaglutide is an alternative. GI side effects; avoid with MTC or MEN2 history.

drugs.name: Tirzepatide
drugs.dose: 2.5 mg SC once weekly for 4 weeks, then increase by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks as needed to a maximum of 15 mg weekly
drugs.notes: Highest glucose and weight efficacy; do not combine with a DPP-4 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA.

drugs.name: Gliclazide MR
drugs.dose: 30 mg orally once daily with breakfast, titrated to a maximum of 120 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Low cost; hypoglycaemia risk, especially in older adults and CKD.

drugs.name: Sitagliptin
drugs.dose: 100 mg orally once daily; 50 mg if eGFR 30 to 44; 25 mg if eGFR below 30

drugs.name: Basal insulin (glargine or NPH)
drugs.dose: 10 units or 0.1 to 0.2 units/kg SC at bedtime, increased by 2 units every 3 days to the fasting goal
drugs.notes: Reduce by 10 to 20% after hypoglycaemia. NPH may need twice-daily dosing.

drugs.name: Atorvastatin
drugs.dose: Moderate intensity 10 to 20 mg once daily; high intensity 40 to 80 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Rosuvastatin 5 to 10 mg (moderate) or 20 to 40 mg (high) is an alternative.
